back_translation: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, according to Shigionoth.
O LORD, I have heard the report of You, and I am afraid. O LORD, revive Your work in the midst of these years; make it known in the midst of these years. In wrath, remember mercy.
God comes from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His splendor covers the heavens, and His praise fills the earth.
His radiance is like the light; rays flash from His hand, and there His power is hidden.
Pestilence goes before Him, and plague goes out at His feet.
He stood and measured the earth; He looked, and the nations trembled. The ancient mountains shattered, the everlasting hills sank low. His ways are eternal.
I saw the tents of Cushan in distress; the tent curtains of the land of Midian trembled.
O LORD, were You angry at the rivers? Was Your wrath against the streams, Your fury against the sea, when You rode on Your horses, on Your chariots of salvation?
You drew Your bow bare; the arrows were ready according to the oath You swore. Selah. You split the earth into rivers.
The mountains saw You and trembled; a torrent of water swept by. The deep roared aloud and lifted its hands on high.
Sun and moon stood still in their dwelling; they moved at the light of Your arrows, at the brightness of Your flashing spear.
You strode through the earth in fury; You trampled the nations in anger.
You went out to save Your people, to save Your anointed. You crushed the head of the house of the wicked, laying it bare from foundation to neck. Selah.
You pierced the head of his warriors with his own spear, when they stormed out to scatter me, exulting as if to devour the poor in secret.
You trampled the sea with Your horses, churning the great waters into foam.

I heard, and my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the sound. Decay entered my bones, and I trembled where I stood. Yet I will wait quietly for the day of distress to come upon the people who invade us.

Though the fig tree does not blossom and there is no fruit on the vines, though the olive crop fails and the fields yield no food, though the flock is cut off from the fold and there is no herd in the stalls—
yet I will exult in the LORD; I will rejoice in the God of my salvation.
The LORD is my strength; He makes my feet like those of a deer, and makes me walk upon my heights. To the choirmaster, with my stringed instruments.
